statement: In Washington, a noncompetition covenant is void and unenforceable against an employee unless its terms were disclosed in writing no later than acceptance of the offer (with independent consideration if entered mid-employment), the employee's annualized earnings from the enforcing party exceed the statutory threshold ($100,000 base, adjusted annually for inflation under RCW 49.62.040), and a laid-off employee is paid base salary for the enforcement period less subsequent earnings; a duration over 18 months is presumed unreasonable (RCW 49.62.020(1)-(2)).
caveat: The operative dollar threshold is the inflation-adjusted figure the Department of Labor & Industries publishes each year, which this rule does not state because it is not in the statute text; verify the current year's figure before relying. Separate rules cover independent contractors and moonlighting.
